skillsNote: The team template carries no skills. Tour Core's seven skills stay in .grok/skills/ for a parked touring account, which reads them from the clone; shipped in this template they put self-guided tours in front of every new host.

integrations.name: Property Core
integrations.auth: OAuth 2.1 discovered from the hosted service. The host signs in or types the invite code from Saad on the approval page and clicks Allow. Grok cannot approve itself. One connection serves every flow.

integrations.name: Cleaner Core
integrations.auth: Added by that flow's own bot, never by the Property Core bot. The host signs in on the approval page, which names the flow, and clicks Allow. Refused unless the account's bots switch is on and the Property Core bot is on Grok Bot.

integrations.name: Supply Core
integrations.auth: Added by that flow's own bot, never by the Property Core bot. The host signs in on the approval page, which names the flow, and clicks Allow. Refused unless the account's bots switch is on and the Property Core bot is on Grok Bot.

integrations.name: Fixer Core
integrations.auth: Added by that flow's own bot, never by the Property Core bot. The host signs in on the approval page, which names the flow, and clicks Allow. Refused unless the account's bots switch is on and the Property Core bot is on Grok Bot.

integrations.name: Google Calendar
integrations.auth: The host connects their own Google account to Grok's built-in Google Calendar connector. Grok reads the events and passes them to Cleaner Core. Cleaner Core never gets a Google approval.

integrations.name: Grok shopping and Vault
integrations.auth: The host's own Grok shopping tools and Vault. Saved cards, Shop Pay, Link, and X Money stay in the host's Vault. Supply Core never sees them.

integrations.name: Google Drive
integrations.auth: The host connects their own Google account to Grok's built-in Drive connector, for Tour Core's portable backups only.

marketplace.activation: A host adds the bot from the team template link and says Set up Property Core, or pastes the prompt into a new bot. It connects to hostedPropertyCoreUrl/mcp, the host signs in or types their invite code from Saad and clicks Allow, then adds a property and picks Cleaner Core, Supply Core, or Fixer Core for it. Each routine is created during setup for the flows turned on. They never run a server.

separateBots.how: With the account's bots switch on, get_state gives the Property Core bot newBots: each flow that runs at a property with no bot of its own. The Property Core bot asks the host once, then creates a bot for each and sends it that flow's firstMessage. Each bot connects at its own address, runs its flow's setup in its own chat, and takes the flow over when it saves its Alerts routine. Every connector on a Grok account shows in every bot, so each bot's instructions name the one connector it uses.
